case_title: Ramanlal Andanr. v. State of Haryana
statutory_provisions: IPC s. 148, 323, 325 and 304 (Part I); IPC s. 302 r/w s. 149
mitigating_circumstances: Incident was without premeditation and a sudden fight upon a sudden quarrel; injuries were inflicted in the heat of passion without taking any undue advantage or acting in a cruel and unusual manner
trial_court_outcome: Convicted all the accused; sentenced to life imprisonment and fines
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction of 4 accused; acquitted the rest
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that on 2nd July 1998, Ved Pal and his brother Gopal were watering their fields in village Doongriwala, district Faridabad. Jai Pal entered their field, and Gopal objected to his trespass. A group of 10 to 12 persons, including Har Chand, Digamber, and Bhagat Singh, arrived and assaulted both Ved Pal and Gopal, causing injuries including a head injury to Gopal that led to his death. The police investigation led to the arrest of several individuals, and the trial court convicted all 10 accused for various offenses, including murder. The High Court acquitted six of the accused, reducing the number of convicted individuals to four. The Supreme Court reviewed the case, noting that the incident was a sudden fight without premeditation and that the injuries were inflicted in the heat of passion. The Court held that the conviction under Section 302 r/w Section 149 was not sustainable and converted the conviction of Har Chand to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 (Part I).
